text: Incident INV-7X4: At commissioning, inverter INV-7X4 reported repeated thermal alarms during sustained load. Airflow around its enclosure was restricted by an adjacent cable tray. Technicians reduced loading, inspected ventilation clearances, and scheduled a controlled retest after the obstruction was addressed. Root cause remained under review pending repeat measurements.

Incident REL-204: Protective relay REL-204 could not complete acceptance testing because approved protection settings were missing from the commissioning package. The engineering team requested a signed settings schedule and postponed sign-off.

Incident GW-12B: Monitoring gateway GW-12B showed inconsistent timestamps relative to the facility meter. Investigators checked network time synchronization, the site clock source, and gateway configuration. The issue must be closed before reliable performance reporting.

Incident CBL-6A: Cable CBL-6A appeared under two different labels in subcontractor documentation. The quality team published a cross-reference mapping and required an as-built drawing update before handover.

Incident ROOF-8Q: Lifting permit ROOF-8Q was delayed because roof point-load approval had not been signed by the structural consultant. Materials were staged at ground level until approved lifting instructions became available.

Incident MTR-3C: Meter MTR-3C had an incomplete interval during a communications outage. Analysts did not invent missing readings; they recorded the missing dates and data limitations in the measurement baseline.
